text: Bulgaria submitted to the European Commission the National Plan for Diversification of Natural Gas Supplies (07.05.2026 13:20)

Bulgaria officially submitted to the European Commission its National Plan for the diversification of natural gas supplies, prepared in accordance with the new European regulation for the phase-out of Russian gas imports, the Ministry of Energy announced. The document presents the country's comprehensive strategy for ensuring secure, sustainable, and competitive supplies, based on alternative sources, new routes, and modernized infrastructure.

The plan places a strong emphasis on the development of the Vertical Gas Corridor, the expansion of interconnections, increasing the capacity of the Chiren UGS, and access to international LNG markets.

With the preparation of the plan, we demonstrated a proactive position, contributing to the fulfillment of the common European goal for energy independence and sustainability, highlighted on this occasion the caretaker Minister of Energy Traicho Traikov, as quoted in the statement. In his words, the document solidifies the country's leadership role in ensuring energy security for the economies and citizens of the Old Continent.

The European Commission was informed that the country is already implementing key measures, including infrastructure projects, optimization of system flexibility, and coordination mechanisms between institutions and operators. The plan emphasizes that the actions taken are fully aligned with the principles of solidarity and the free movement of gas within the EU.

With this strategic document, Bulgaria shows that it is acting in a timely and consistent manner, in full compliance with European goals, by turning diversification into a real, measurable, and sustainable policy, Minister Traykov added. The country demonstrates that it has concrete projects, clear deadlines, and a stable vision for the future of the energy system.

The submission of the plan highlights Bulgaria's role as a reliable partner in the regional energy architecture and an active participant in the construction of a modern, connected, and competitive infrastructure. The document sends a clear signal that the country is working consistently to reduce dependencies, increase security of supply, and strengthen the resilience of the European energy market.

With the presentation of the National Plan, Bulgaria reaffirms its commitment to common European goals and proves that it is turning political priorities into concrete actions that have a real effect on the country and the region, the Ministry of Energy added.
